scenes.title: A normal day for Leo
scenes.captureAction: Restore the early film-world to film-shop zoom and merchant reveal from the accepted aerial version; retain the current story and later WHO/WHAT emphasis.
scenes.narration: It was a normal day for Leo. His shop was ready, but customers kept walking. For days, he faced the same question: who should he reach, and what should he offer? The clues were there, scattered across shopper activity, product interest and payments.

scenes.title: What Market Metro is
scenes.captureAction: Introduce Market Metro as an AI commerce environment using the actual market view and Observe, Train, Test and Measure stages. Do not show ontology as the product itself.
scenes.narration: Could AI do this for Leo? Meet Market Metro: a simulated commerce environment where AI agents analyze shopper behavior, train models and test marketing campaigns. We measure how their decisions change purchases, merchant contribution and PayPal payment outcomes.
onScreen: A commerce world for AI agents

scenes.title: The right data for the question
scenes.captureAction: The ontology routes recommendation and inquiry history separately, while distinguishing input features from later outcome labels.
scenes.narration: The ontology gives that data meaning. It connects shoppers, products, contacts and payments, then maps each prediction to the right training examples. Recommendations and inquiries stay separate. Earlier signals can be inputs; later outcomes are reserved for labels and evaluation.

scenes.title: From understanding to action
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: The agent studies demand and available stock, chooses twenty eight days of history, and asks local tools to train two models. Its decision summary, tool calls and results become checkpoints you can inspect.

scenes.title: Test before sending
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Before a campaign launches, the verifier tests the candidate models in matching development markets. It checks PayPal and merchant outcomes, then publishes an eligible tested configuration or keeps the current policy.

scenes.title: The recommendation becomes a purchase
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: On day thirty five, a recommendation reaches our quiet shopper. They buy a ninety six dollar side table, and it arrives the next day. Fixed rules left that same request unfilled.

scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: PayPal Sandbox captures that exact order. Its receipt records ninety six dollars gross, the provider fee and merchant proceeds. Those records link back to the warehouse, so the proof is traceable without counting another sale.

scenes.narration: Across the same market, sixteen more purchases were completed and kept. Payment volume grows by two thousand three hundred forty-five dollars. Merchant contribution and modeled PayPal net both rise, after AI cost. The numbers on screen compare against the same fixed rules.

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
